title: Regrouping filtered colimits by bounded filtered subcategories
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ as in [def-weil-size-convention], and use ordinary categories and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ be an uncountable regular cardinal: a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets each of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. Let $J$ be a small filtered category, meaning every finite diagram, including the empty diagram, admits a cocone. Let $P_J$ be the poset of subcategories $J'\subseteq J$ which are filtered and have fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms; these subcategories need not be full, and the order is inclusion on objects and arrows. Every set of fewer than $\lambda$ arrows of $J$ is contained in some member of $P_J$. The poset $P_J$ is small, nonempty and $\lambda$-directed: every family of fewer than $\lambda$ members has an upper bound. For every locally small category $\mathcal A$ with all small colimits and every functor $X:J\to\mathcal A$, restriction and the colimit cocones give a canonical isomorphism
$$\operatorname{colim}_{J'\in P_J}\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J'}X(j)\ \cong\ \operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}X(j).$$
The outer diagram uses the canonical colimit maps induced by inclusions of subcategories.

source.place: Proof of Theorem B.0.20, accessibility argument; agent refinement of the filtered-colimit step for the sufficiently filtered variant. This general regrouping lemma is extracted from the retained proof, not asserted to be a named theorem in HA. No Stacks tag is assigned.

proof.text: Let $S$ be a set of fewer than $\lambda$ arrows. Choose $j_0\in J$ using filtered nonemptiness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Put $E_0=S\cup\{1_{j_0}\}$ and let $O_n$ be the set of endpoints of arrows in $E_n$. Recursively form an increasing sequence of arrow sets. To obtain $E_{n+1}$ retain $E_n$ and adjoin: $1_x$ for every $x\in O_n$; $g\circ f$ for every composable pair $f,g\in E_n$; two chosen arrows $x\to z_{x,y}$ and $y\to z_{x,y}$ for every $(x,y)\in O_n^2$; and one chosen arrow $h_{f,g}:y\to z_{f,g}$ with $h_{f,g}f=h_{f,g}g$ for every parallel pair $f,g:x\to y$ in $E_n$. The last two choices exist by the two filteredness conditions in the cited definition. They are choices from sets because $J$ is small. Define $E=\bigcup_{n<\omega}E_n$ and $O=\bigcup_{n<\omega}O_n$. This construction adds only the displayed witnesses, not every arrow between the selected objects.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: Every $E_n$ has size less than $\lambda$. For the base this follows from $|S|<\lambda$ and adjoining one element. Inductively put $\theta=\max(\aleph_0,|E_n|)<\lambda$, using uncountability. The endpoints satisfy $|O_n|\leq 2|E_n|\leq\theta$. By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power], $\theta\cdot\theta=\theta$. Thus each of the composable-pair, object-pair and parallel-pair indexing sets in step 1 has size at most $\theta$; each index contributes at most two arrows. The finite union of these families still has size at most $\theta$: finite disjoint labels and an extra binary choice embed into a finite subset of $\theta$, and then into $\theta\times\theta$. Hence $|E_{n+1}|\leq\theta<\lambda$. Finally $\omega<\lambda$ and the assumed regular-union property give $|E|<\lambda$. This is induction on $n$, followed by one countable union, with no assumption that the full subcategory on $O$ is small in cardinality.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: The sets $O,E$ define a subcategory $K\subseteq J$: every object in $O$ acquires its identity at a later stage, and any composable pair in $E$ belongs to some common $E_n$ and acquires its composite in $E_{n+1}$. Its laws are those of $J$. It is nonempty because it contains $j_0$. For two objects, or two parallel arrows, a common finite stage contains them, so the next stage supplies the common target, or the equalizing arrow, inside $K$. These are precisely the three filteredness conditions of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. To see the finite-diagram formulation directly, first send the finitely many diagram objects to a common object by repeatedly using the two-object condition. For each diagram arrow, equalize the two resulting parallel maps into that object, postcomposing all legs each time. There are finitely many arrows, and postcomposition preserves equations already imposed. The empty diagram uses $j_0$. Thus $K$ is filtered, has fewer than $\lambda$ arrows by step 2, and contains $S$.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: A subcategory of the small category $J$ is specified by subsets of its object and arrow sets satisfying identity and composition closure. The collection of such pairs is a subset of the product of two small power sets, so $P_J$ is small in the chosen universe of [def-weil-size-convention]; inclusion is a partial order. Applying steps 1-3 to $S=\varnothing$ proves nonemptiness. Given a family $(K_a)_{a\in A}$ in $P_J$ with $|A|<\lambda$, regularity bounds $S=\bigcup_a\operatorname{Mor}(K_a)$ by $\lambda$. Apply steps 1-3 to this $S$. The resulting member contains every $K_a$, including its objects because each object's identity belongs to $S$. It is an upper bound. This proves $\lambda$-directedness, including the empty family; finite directedness follows since $\lambda$ is infinite. Applying step 3 to singleton arrow sets also shows that every arrow of $J$, and every object via its identity, occurs in a member.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: For $K\in P_J$ choose $Y_K=\operatorname{colim}_{j\in K}X(j)$ with coprojections $i_{K,j}$. All these colimits exist because $K$ is small and $\mathcal A$ has all small colimits. For an inclusion $K\subseteq H$, the cocone $(i_{H,j})_{j\in K}$ induces a unique $t_{K,H}:Y_K\to Y_H$ with $t_{K,H}i_{K,j}=i_{H,j}$, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The identity on $Y_K$ has this property for $K=H$, so $t_{K,K}=1$; for $K\subseteq H\subseteq R$, both $t_{H,R}t_{K,H}$ and $t_{K,R}$ have this property, so they are equal. This constructs exactly the outer diagram in the statement. Its small colimit $L=\operatorname{colim}_{K\in P_J}Y_K$ exists by step 4; write $k_K:Y_K\to L$ for its coprojections.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: Write $C=\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}X(j)$ and $a_j:X(j)\to C$ for its coprojections. For each $K$, restriction induces $q_K:Y_K\to C$ with $q_Ki_{K,j}=a_j$, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $K\subseteq H$, both $q_Ht_{K,H}$ and $q_K$ have the same composites with all $i_{K,j}$ and hence agree. Thus the $q_K$ form an outer cocone and give the canonical map $q:L\to C$ with $qk_K=q_K$.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: For each $j\in J$ choose $K\in P_J$ containing $j$, using step 4, and set $b_j=k_Ki_{K,j}:X(j)\to L$. This is independent of the choice: if $H$ also contains $j$, choose a common upper bound $R$ in $P_J$. The equations $k_Rt_{K,R}=k_K$ and $t_{K,R}i_{K,j}=i_{R,j}$ give $k_Ki_{K,j}=k_Ri_{R,j}$, and the same calculation for $H$ gives equality. For any arrow $f:j\to j'$, choose a member $K$ containing $f$, by step 3. Both endpoints lie in $K$, so independence allows computation there: $b_{j'}X(f)=k_Ki_{K,j'}X(f)=k_Ki_{K,j}=b_j$. Hence $b$ is a cocone on $X$, and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] supplies $r:C\to L$ with $ra_j=b_j$.

source.place: Tags 002V (definition-directed) and 002F (definition-colimit); agent-written bounded non-full closure and cocone argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: For each $j$, choosing $K$ containing it gives $qra_j=qb_j=qk_Ki_{K,j}=a_j$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore gives $qr=1_C$. Conversely, for every $K$ and $j\in K$, $rqk_Ki_{K,j}=ra_j=b_j=k_Ki_{K,j}$. Inner colimit uniqueness gives $rqk_K=k_K$ for every $K$, and outer colimit uniqueness gives $rq=1_L$. Thus the canonical $q$ of step 6 is an isomorphism with inverse $r$. It has precisely the specified compatibility with both colimit cocones. This proves the claimed canonical isomorphism without invoking a cofinality theorem or identifying ordinary colimits with coherent colimits.

lean.statement: theorem filteredColimit_cardinal_regrouping (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : κ.IsRegular) (huncountable : Cardinal.aleph0 < κ) (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] : (∀ (S : Set (Σ x y : J, x ⟶ y)), Cardinal.mk S < κ → ∃ K : BoundedFilteredSubcategory J κ, S ⊆ K.val.arrows) ∧ Nonempty (BoundedFilteredSubcategory J κ) ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) (K : I → BoundedFilteredSubcategory J κ), Cardinal.mk I < κ → ∃ L : BoundedFilteredSubcategory J κ, ∀ i : I, K i ≤ L) ∧ (∀ (A : Type v) [Category.{w} A] [Limits.HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} A] (X : J ⥤ A), IsIso (BoundedFilteredSubcategory.comparison (κ := κ) X))
